Stepping and error control

Source: vignettes/articles/methods-stepping.Rmd
methods-stepping.Rmd

Arguments: method, useNDF and sparse of cppODE(); abstol, reltol, maxOrder, stald and sensErrCon of solveODE(). Symbols follow the notation table.

Initial-value problem

cppODE() solves \[ \dot{x} = f(x, p, t), \qquad x(t_0) = x_0, \tag{1} \] with \(f\) explicit in time for forcings. Step \(n\) advances \(x_n\) at \(t_n\) to \(x_{n+1}\) at \(t_{n+1} = t_n + h_n\) (coefficients).

Stiffness and the choice of method

On \(\dot y = \lambda y\), \(\lambda \in \mathbb{C}^-\), a one-step method multiplies \(y\) per step by \(R(z)\), \(z = h \lambda\). The method is

  • A-stable if \(|R(z)| \le 1\) on the left half-plane, so the solution decays with the exact one at any step size;
  • A(\(\varphi\))-stable if the bound holds on the wedge \(\{ z \in \mathbb{C} : |\arg(-z)| \le \varphi \}\) for some \(\varphi < 90^{\circ}\);
  • L-stable if A-stable with \(R(z) \to 0\) as \(\operatorname{Re}(z) \to -\infty\), which damps very stiff transients within one step.

Problem (1) is stiff when stability, not accuracy, limits an explicit step: \(h \lambda_k\), \(\lambda_k\) the eigenvalues of \(J\) along the trajectory, must stay in the stability domain. Stiffness depends on spectrum, horizon and tolerance; kinetic networks with rate constants over orders of magnitude and many discretized parabolic PDEs are stiff. BDF/NDF and Rosenbrock4, stable on the left half-plane or a wide wedge of it, suit stiff problems; Adams-Moulton and Tsit5 do not, at any tolerance. An explicit method fails or takes uneconomic steps on a stiff problem, an implicit one costs a constant overhead per step on a non-stiff problem; BDF/NDF is the default, with sparse = TRUE for large sparse Jacobians.

Multistep methods

A linear multistep method of order \(q\) combines \(\{x_{n+1-j}, f_{n+1-j}\}_{j=0}^{q}\) linearly, with few right-hand-side evaluations per step. cppDE stores BDF and Adams in the Nordsieck form of SUNDIALS [1], the scaled derivative array at \(t_n\) in place of the past \(q+1\) states, \[ z =\left(x_n,\, h_n \dot{x}_n,\, \dfrac{h_n^2}{2!} \ddot{x}_n, \,\dots,\, \dfrac{h_n^{q}}{q!} x_n^{(q)} \right). \] A change of step size or order is a linear transformation of \(z\), not a refit.

Backward Differentiation Formula (bdf)

The BDF of order \(q\) defines \(x_{n+1}\) implicitly by \[ \sum_{j=0}^{q} \alpha_j\, x_{n+1-j} \;=\; h_n\, f(x_{n+1}, t_{n+1}), \tag{2} \] exact for polynomials of degree \(\le q\) on the past \(q+1\) nodes; A-stable for \(q \le 2\), A(\(\varphi\))-stable for \(q \in \{3,4,5\}\) with \(\varphi\) from \(86^\circ\) (\(q=3\)) to \(51^\circ\) (\(q=5\)).

The corrector (2) is solved by simplified Newton iteration, \[ W \Delta x^{(\nu)} = - s\, \tilde r \left(x_{n+1}^{(\nu)}\right), \qquad x_{n+1}^{(\nu+1)} = x_{n+1}^{(\nu)} + \Delta x^{(\nu)}, \tag{3} \] with \(\tilde r\) the residual of (2) divided by \(h_n \beta_0\), \(\beta_0 = 1/\alpha_0\), and iteration matrix \[ W = \frac{1}{\gamma_p}I - J\bigl(x_s, t_s\bigr), \tag{4} \] in the SUNDIALS form [1], \((I - \gamma_p J)/\gamma_p\). \(J\) is taken at the predicted \(x_s\), \(t_s\) of the step that last evaluated it; \(\gamma_p\) is \(h\beta_0\) at the last factorization. With \(\gamma = h_n\beta_0\) of the current step, the scale \(s = (\gamma/\gamma_p)\, 2/(1 + \gamma/\gamma_p)\) (BDF) or \(s = \gamma/\gamma_p\) (Adams) restores the step of a factorization at \(\gamma\), as in CVODE. Factorizing \(W\) dominates the step cost and is reused across steps.

The default Numerical Differentiation Formula (NDF) [2] adds to the BDF corrector a multiple \(\kappa_q H_q\,(x_{n+1} - x_{n+1}^{\mathrm{pred}})\) of the Nordsieck predictor error, \(H_q = \sum_{m=1}^{q} 1/m\) (BDF and NDF coefficients). The term scales \(1/(h_n\beta_0)\) in (4) by \((1 - \kappa_q)\) and the leading truncation-error coefficient \(1/(q+1)\) by \(1 + \kappa_q (q+1) H_q\). With \(\kappa_q < 0\) the step at equal accuracy grows by \(26\,\%\) over BDF for \(q \le 3\) and \(12\,\%\) for \(q = 4\) [2], at a small loss of stability angle. useNDF = FALSE gives BDF (\(\kappa_q \equiv 0\)).

The corrector takes at most three iterations, each one right-hand-side evaluation and one linear solve, and converges at \(\delta\,\min(1, \rho)/\tau_q \le 1\), with \(\delta\) the WRMS norm of the latest correction, \(\rho\) the estimated contraction rate and \(\tau_q\) an order-dependent constant. As in CVODE:

  • \(W\) is refactorized when \(h_n\beta_0\) has moved by more than \(30\,\%\) since the last factorization, after \(20\) steps, or after a failed corrector or error test;
  • \(J\) is re-evaluated at a refactorization once it is \(51\) steps old, and after a failed corrector;
  • with the old Jacobian, a sparse \(W\) changes only on the diagonal.

Like the step size, \(W\) is a solver decision: forward sensitivities and the reverse sweep iterate against \(W\) without differentiating it, and so differentiate the computed solution (Forward sensitivities, Reverse mode).

Adams-Moulton (adams)

Adams-Moulton integrates the interpolant of \(f\) through \(\{(t_{n+1-j}, f_{n+1-j})\}_{j=0}^{q}\) over \([t_n, t_{n+1}]\), \[ x_{n+1} \;=\; x_n \;+\; h_n \sum_{j=0}^{q} \beta_j\, f(x_{n+1-j}, t_{n+1-j}), \tag{5} \] implicit through the \(j=0\) term. As in CVODES with a linear solver, cppDE applies the BDF Newton iteration on (4) with the Adams weight \(\beta_0\): same setup triggers, Jacobian reuse, convergence test and controller, other coefficients and \(q_{\max} = 12\). The stability domain shrinks with order and for \(q \ge 3\) contains no wedge of \(\mathbb{C}^-\), so Adams suits non-stiff, smooth problems over long horizons. The Newton corrector keeps a mildly stiff component from stalling the iteration, but the stability domain still bounds the step.

Single-step methods

Single-step methods keep only the current state, reach order \(q > 1\) through internal stages, and restart at full order after an event, where multistep methods rebuild the Nordsieck history from order \(1\).

Rosenbrock (rb4)

A Rosenbrock method linearizes the implicit Runge-Kutta condition about \((x_n, t_n)\); the \(s\) stages \(k_i\) solve \[ W k_i = f\left(x_n + \sum_{j<i} \alpha_{ij}\, k_j,\, t_n + c_i\, h_n \right) + \dfrac{1}{h_n} \sum_{j<i} \gamma_{ij}\, k_j + h_n\, d_i\, \dfrac{\partial f}{\partial t}(x_n, t_n), \tag{6} \] with iteration matrix \[ W = \frac{1}{\gamma\, h_n}I - J(x_n, t_n). \tag{7} \]

Rosenbrock method coefficients.
symbol meaning
\(\alpha_{ij}\) weights of earlier stages \(k_j\), \(j<i\), in stage \(i\)
\(c_i\) time abscissa of stage \(i\)
\(\gamma_{ij}\) weights of earlier stages in the linear-solve correction of stage \(i\)
\(\gamma\) diagonal coefficient in \(W\)
\(d_i\) weights of the explicit time dependence \(\partial f/\partial t\)
\(m_i\) weights of the advanced solution \(x_{n+1}\)
\(\hat{m}_i\) weights of the embedded order-3 estimator for step control

The advanced solution and embedded estimate are \[ x_{n+1} = x_n + \sum_{i=1}^{s} m_i\, k_i, \qquad \hat{x}_{n+1} \;=\; x_n + \sum_{i=1}^{s} \hat{m}_i\, k_i. \] Each stage (6) is one linear solve, no Newton iteration; an accepted step costs one \(J\), one factorization of \(W\), five right-hand-side evaluations and six back-substitutions. The order-\(4\) coefficients of Hairer and Wanner [3, Sec. IV.7], also used by the rosenbrock4 stepper of Boost.Numeric.Odeint, form an L-stable pair with an embedded order-\(3\) estimator. Rosenbrock4 competes with BDF on stiff problems with a cheap Jacobian and suits frequent state discontinuities at moderate dimension.

Tsitouras (tsit5)

The explicit \(5(4)\) pair of Tsitouras [4] assumes only the first column simplifying condition, \[ \sum_{i=1}^{s} b_i\, a_{ij} \;=\; b_j\,(1 - c_j), \qquad j = 1, \dots, s, \] not the row condition \(\sum_{j} a_{ij}\, c_j = c_i^2/2\), \(i \ge 3\), of the Dormand-Prince pair. The freed parameters lower the leading-error norm; the coefficients meet the column condition to rounding and violate the row condition. The \(s = 7\) stages are First-Same-As-Last (FSAL), \[ k_7 \;=\; f(x_{n+1},\, t_n + h_n) \;=\; k_1 \text{ at step } n+1, \] so an accepted step costs six right-hand-side evaluations.

Symbols of the Tsit5 tableau.
symbol meaning
\(a_{ij}\) weights of earlier stages in stage \(i\) (strictly lower triangular)
\(c_i\) time abscissa of stage \(i\), \(c_i = \sum_{j<i} a_{ij}\)
\(b_i\) weights of the order-5 solution; \(b_7 = 0\)
\(\hat{b}_i\) weights of the embedded order-4 estimator; \(\hat{b}_7 \ne 0\)
\(k_i\) stage \(i\): \(k_i = f\!\left(x_n + h_n\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}k_j,\; t_n + c_i h_n\right)\)

The advanced solution, embedded estimate and local error estimate are \[ x_{n+1} = x_n + h_n \sum_{i=1}^{7} b_i\, k_i, \qquad \hat{x}_{n+1} = x_n + h_n \sum_{i=1}^{7} \hat{b}_i\, k_i, \] \[ e_{n+1} = h_n \sum_{i=1}^{7} (\hat{b}_i - b_i)\, k_i. \] Without Jacobian or linear solve, Tsit5 advances furthest per right-hand-side evaluation of the four methods and suits non-stiff problems with an expensive right-hand side.

Adaptive step-size control

The error estimate is reduced to a scalar by the weighted root-mean-square norm \[ \| e_{n+1} \|_{\mathrm{WRMS}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n_x} \sum_{j=1}^{n_x} \left( \frac{e_{n+1,j}}{w_{j}} \right)^{\!2}}, \qquad w_{j} = \mathtt{abstol} + \mathtt{reltol}\,|x^{\mathrm{ref}}_{j}|, \tag{8} \] where \(x^{\mathrm{ref}}\) is \(x_n\) in BDF/NDF and Adams, as in CVODE, and \(\max(|x_n|, |x_{n+1}|)\) componentwise in the single-step methods. A step is accepted when \(\| e_{n+1} \|_{\mathrm{WRMS}} \le 1\).

The single-step methods use the proportional-integral (PI) controller of [3]. With \(\varepsilon_{n+1} = \| e_{n+1} \|_{\mathrm{WRMS}}\) and \(\hat q\) the embedded order (\(3\) Rosenbrock4, \(4\) Tsit5), an accepted step sets \[ h_{n+1} = h_n\, \min\Bigl\{\rho_{\max},\; \max\Bigl(\rho_{\min},\; S\, \varepsilon_{n+1}^{-(k_P+k_I)}\, \varepsilon_{n}^{\,k_I}\Bigr)\Bigr\}, \qquad k_P = \frac{0.7}{\hat q+1}, \quad k_I = \frac{0.4}{\hat q+1}, \] with \(S = 0.9\), \(\rho_{\min} = 0.2\), \(\rho_{\max} = 5\), and \(\varepsilon_{n}\) the norm of the previous accepted step, floored at \(0.01\). The first step and the first accepted step after a rejection use the integral factor \(S\,\varepsilon_{n+1}^{-1/(\hat q+1)}\), capped at \(1\) after a rejection. A rejected step is retried with \(S\,\varepsilon_{n+1}^{-1/(\hat q+1)}\) clamped to \([\rho_{\min}, 0.9]\).

The multistep methods select step size and order as CVODE. With \(E_{q'}\) the error norm at order \(q'\), the candidate ratios are \[ \eta_{q'} = \frac{1}{\bigl(B_{q'}\, E_{q'}\bigr)^{1/(q'+1)} + 10^{-6}}, \qquad q' \in \{q-1,\, q,\, q+1\}, \] with \(B_{q-1} = B_q = 6\) and \(B_{q+1} = 10\). Neighboring orders are compared \(q+1\) steps after a change to order \(q\) and every second step at unchanged order; the largest ratio fixes the next order. A ratio below \(1.5\) leaves \(h\) unchanged; the cap is \(10^4\) on the first step, \(10\) afterwards.

The order is at most \(q_{\max}\) (\(5\) for BDF/NDF, \(12\) for Adams) or a smaller maxOrder. For \(q \ge 3\) the stability domain excludes a wedge around the imaginary axis; at the edge of this domain the error test rejects steps and shrinks \(h\) where a lower order would be stable. stald = TRUE adds CVODE stability limit detection to the BDF family [1]:

  • from order \(3\) on, each step records the squared norms of the scaled derivatives of degree \(q-1\), \(q\) (Nordsieck columns) and \(q+1\) (corrector correction);
  • after \(q+5\) steps at order \(q\), the last five records give the magnitude \(r\) of the dominant root of step-to-step error propagation;
  • \(r > 0.98\) lowers the order by one at step size \(\eta_{q-1} h_n\), overriding the order selection unless that already lowers the order.

Off by default as in CVODE, it saves steps on weakly damped stiff oscillations and costs the estimate on every step. On a cvode() model, maxOrder and stald set CVodeSetMaxOrd and CVodeSetStabLimDet.

The first step

The single-step methods follow [5], Algorithm II.4.4. A rough \(h_{\mathrm{s}} = 0.01\,\|x_0\| / \|f_0\|\), \(f_0 = f(x_0, p, t_0)\), fixes a scale, the second derivative \(\ddot x\) along the trajectory fixes the curvature, and \[ h_{\mathrm{c}} = \left( \frac{0.01}{\max\bigl(\|f_0\|, \|\ddot x\|\bigr)} \right)^{\!1/2} \tag{9} \] combines the two. The exponent is that of a first-order method: \(\|\ddot x\|\) stands in for the derivative of order \(p+1\), exact only at \(p = 1\); higher orders raise the step within a few steps. Generated code gives \(\ddot x = \partial f/\partial t + J f\), the derivative of \(f\) along \((f, 1)\). Norms are weighted maximum norms, weights \(\mathtt{abstol} + \mathtt{reltol}\,|x_0|\), including the sensitivities with sensErrCon = TRUE. The step is \(\min(100\,h_{\mathrm{s}},\, h_{\mathrm{c}},\, h_{\mathrm{ub}})\). The upper bound \(h_{\mathrm{ub}}\), at most a tenth of the interval, keeps one Euler step from changing any component by more than a fraction of the component scale; a lower bound keeps \(t_0 + h \ne t_0\) in double precision.

The multistep methods use the bounds of CVODES cvHin: \(h_{\mathrm{lb}}\) above the rounding of the time variable, the same \(h_{\mathrm{ub}}\), and the step \(\sqrt{2/\|\ddot x\|}\) in the weighted RMS norm if below \(h_{\mathrm{ub}}\), else \(h_{\mathrm{lb}}^{1/4} h_{\mathrm{ub}}^{3/4}\), halved and clamped to the bounds. cvHin estimates \(\ddot x\) by differences of \(f\) over trial steps until two estimates agree, one round with the exact \(\ddot x\). After every event each method estimates a new first step from the post-event state.

Dense output

Each accepted step interpolates output times inside the step without right-hand-side evaluations. With \(\tau = (t - t_n)/h_n \in [0, 1]\):

  • Tsit5: the cubic Hermite interpolant through \(x_n\), \(x_{n+1}\) and the FSAL derivatives \(k_1\), \(k_7\), \[ x(t) = (1+2\tau)(1-\tau)^2\, x_n + \tau^2(3-2\tau)\, x_{n+1} + \tau(1-\tau)^2\, h_n k_1 + \tau^2(\tau-1)\, h_n k_7 . \]
  • Rosenbrock4: the stage-based cubic of Hairer and Wanner [3], \[ x(t) = (1-\tau)\, x_n + \tau\bigl(x_{n+1} + (1-\tau)(u_3 + \tau\, u_4)\bigr), \qquad u_3 = \sum_{i=1}^{5} d_i^{(2)} k_i, \quad u_4 = \sum_{i=1}^{5} d_i^{(3)} k_i, \] with the dense-output coefficients.
  • BDF/NDF and Adams: the Nordsieck polynomial of degree \(q\) after the step, slots \(z_j\) at \(t_{n+1}\) scaled with \(h_n\), \[ x(t) = \sum_{j=0}^{q} z_{j}\, \Bigl(\frac{t - t_{n+1}}{h_n}\Bigr)^{j}. \]

The interpolant order is \(3\) for the single-step methods, below the step order (\(5\) Tsit5, \(4\) Rosenbrock4), and \(q\) for the multistep methods.
